turns.text: The tomatoes from Dad's plants came in this week. I picked the first ones on Sunday, which is when he used to call.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I was glad they were ready. Then I kept thinking I should send him a picture. It felt nice having something from him, but it hurt too.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: You felt happy to have the tomatoes, and then the old instinct to share them with him made the loss hurt. It’s lovely that something he grew is still part of your life, even when it brings both feelings. What do you miss most about those calls?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Mostly just hearing his voice. We didn’t even talk about anything important. He’d ask how the week was going, and somehow Sundays felt less empty after.

turns.speaker: helper

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I still catch myself waiting for the phone to ring. Then I remember. I try to keep busy, but that part of the day feels pretty quiet.

turns.speaker: helper

You’ve been carrying that moment week after week, and I’m glad you’re letting me hear about it. Would it feel comforting to tell me about something he used to say on those calls?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: He always asked if I was eating enough. I used to tease him about it. I miss that more than I expected.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: That little question was one of the ways he showed he cared, and now it carries so much tenderness. It makes sense you miss it more than you expected. What did you usually say when you teased him?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I’d say, “Yes, Dad, I’m not going to starve.” He’d laugh and tell me he was just checking. I can almost hear him saying it now.

turns.speaker: helper
turns.text: You can almost hear his laugh and that familiar “just checking.” There’s so much love in that ordinary exchange. I’m glad you shared it with me. What does it feel like to hear his voice in your memory right now?
